recipes.name: Homemade Sloppy Joes
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Place ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium heat; cook and stir until beef is browned and crumbled, about 10 minutes.
Stir in green pepper and garlic; cook and stir until softened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1 cup water and stir, scraping the pan to dissolve any brown flavor bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in ketchup, brown sugar, Dijon mustard, salt, black pepper, and Worcestershire sauce.
Add remaining 1 cup water and bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until liquid has evaporated and mixture is thick, about 40 minutes.
Season with salt, black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and cayenne pepper. Serve and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Sloppy Joes
raw_recipe.description: These homemade sloppy joes are made with ground beef, onion, pepper, and ketchup. A thick and rich filling makes these iconic sandwiches easy to eat.

video.description: Join us on a culinary adventure as we unveil the secrets to creating the ultimate Sloppy Joes. In this delectable video, we'll take you through the step-by-step process of crafting a mouthwatering sandwich that will satisfy your cravings. Discover how to perfectly brown ground beef, infuse it with a rich and tangy homemade sauce, and pile it high on soft hamburger buns. We'll share our tips for achieving the ideal balance of sweet and savory flavors that make Sloppy Joes a timeless comfort food favorite. Whether you're hosting a casual gathering or seeking a quick and delicious meal, this Sloppy Joes recipe is guaranteed to bring smiles to every bite. Get ready to indulge in a classic delight that never goes out of style!

review.reviewBody: No more Manwich for my family! My family loved this recipie--I just added a splash of cider vinegar for an extra tang! Perfect. Thanks Chef John-Cant wait to try more of your recipies.

Better than anything canned! I substitute Swerve brown sugar and Heinz No-Sugar-Added. Totally delicious. I use an ice cream scoop to portion servings into individual zipper bags and freeze them. They reheat perfectly.

On the open face burger buns, spread butter and garlic salt. Heat lightly in a Grill (in foil on the upper level) or toaster oven. This will add a subtle increase in flavor to the overall taste of The Sloppy Joes.
Did not care for this. I think I would use regular mustard and cut the brown sugar by 2/3rds.

I made this recipe as directed except for adding 1 lb of ground turkey. I liked it but felt it need more flavor to make that “sloppy joe” taste come to life. 3/4 cup more of ketchup and 2 tsp of chili powder made this just perfect! I recommend only using 1 cup of water to avoid having to simmer sooooo long to get the sauce to thicken. Definitely use very lean meat.

This was really good. My husband does not like it to be sweet so I left the sugar out and used tomato paste instead of ketchup. I only used 1 cup of water and did not simmer for 45 minutes. Once it reached the consistency I liked I served it up. Everyone was happy with it.

I tried this recipe because I couldn't remember Moms recipe. Wasn't as sweet or tangy as her's was. Soooo, I added 1 more T of brown sugar and 1/4 c of ketchup, simmered on the stove and it was close to Mom's. Oh, and I added a thick slice of Velvetta cheese, rewaŕmed in my microwave, and enjoyed a GREAT sandwich! Thank you!

The sauce was much too sweet for us. Easily fixed w vinegar & hot sauce. The sauce was at the correct consistency before adding the water. I already omitted the cup of water w the veggies because it served no purpose. I wish I had not added the other cup of water to the sauce because it tasted like VERY watered down sauce. Luckily, I heated it up in a saucepan before adding to the cooked IMPOSSIBLE plant based ground "meat", to melt the sugar (which was not needed being so sweet), so I was able to fix it with double the sauce ingredients. Minus the water of course. Even then it was still watery but at least edible. Also, always cook your veggies until almost done to carmelize BEFORE the meat. Remove from pan, add meat, cook half way or so, then add veggies. Never add water to sauteed veggies, you'll just end up with soggy, no flavour veggies.

Best Sloppies I've ever had! Full of amazing flavor!! I added less water to it and it was still too runny. This time I will only add approximately 1/4 cup to hamburger before adding ketchup sauce and none to sauce. I'm making Shepherds Pie today and using this for the plain hamburger bottom layer, plus adding a layer of fresh corn between this and the mashed potatoes. We can't wait!!

This recipe was simple and easy to make. Although I normally sauté my vegetables with the meat (I substituted ground turkey for chuck/round/sirloin), and seasoned it with a bit of Lawry's salt and black pepper. I followed directions pretty well until I got to 2 tbsp. brown sugar. I didn't have time to soften 2 tbsp. so I did 1 tbsp. brown sugar, the other honey. Needless to say the meat mixture was extremely sweet, but good nonetheless. I'll definitely make this again, sans the honey! ***Ooops, I forgot to add cayenne, which would have given this meat mixture a li'l personality! 😉
Just wasted a 1.5lbs of ground beef to make sloppy soup. If you are following this recipe, do not use 2 cups of water.
I did not add the brown sugar, I found it sweet enough (almost too sweet) with the 3/4 cup of Heinz ketchup. It was really good!
I followed the directions except didn’t add all of the 2nd cup of water. I’ve made it many times and it’s always good to!
A little more heat would have been good

My husband has been a marriage-long hater of sloppy joes. Yes, I know - the mind boggles. But I had a craving and made this recipe (without the green peppers). Big BIG hit!! He loved it. His entire plate was clean. Hooray!! This recipe is delicious. Thank you!
It doesn't have enough ketchup for my taste.
Followed the recipe, except glad I only added 1 cup of water. I also added more ketchup and 1 teaspoon of chilli powder. Let it simmer till it got thick. Excellent
Made it as written. I'll go back to the recipe I've used for the past fifty years.
Teen son had 2. I used onion & poppy seed buns .... YUM. Drain meat after browning. 3/4 c water.
I love sloppy joes and thankful for Chef Johns video instructions with special tips! Watching the video and instructions makes a difference!
